question: When Rome granted a household the right to draw aqueduct water, what exactly did the grant fix?
answer: The bore of a bronze nozzle, not the flow. Frontinus, water commissioner from AD 97, calls each grant a calix: a stamped bronze pipe of set size, fitted where the private pipe left the tank. Flow depends on depth too; he warns that one set lower draws more. Rome sold water by the hole.
move: Ask whether the thing measured is the thing being paid for.
reference: Frontinus, De Aquaeductu Urbis Romae, ed. R. H. Rodgers, Cambridge University Press, 2004
